title: Binary compatibility of recursive comparisons for a positive endofunctor family
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category [def-nagata-category]. For every positive integer $r$ let $P_r:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ be an endofunctor, and put $T=P_1$. Use the powers of [def-trf-endofunctor-powers], with $T^1=T$ and $T^{r+1}=T\circ T^r$. Composition is in functional order. A natural transformation $u:F\Rightarrow G$ means maps $u_M:F(M)\to G(M)$ with $G(f)\circ u_M=u_N\circ F(f)$ for every $f:M\to N$; a natural isomorphism has invertible components. For a transformation $u$, write $(uH)_M=u_{H(M)}$ and $(H(u))_M=H(u_M)$. All iterated compositions are compared by the canonical functor associators, whose components are identity maps.
For all positive $a,b$ suppose given natural isomorphisms $C_{a,b}:P_{a+b}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_a\circ P_b$ satisfying, for every positive $a,b,c$,
$$P_a(C_{b,c})\circ C_{a,b+c}=(C_{a,b}P_c)\circ C_{a+b,c}.$$
Define transformations recursively by
$$d_1=\mathrm{id}_T,\qquad d_{r+1}=T(d_r)\circ C_{1,r}.$$
Then each $d_r:P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}T^r$ is a natural isomorphism, and for every positive $a,b$ one has the equality of natural transformations
$$d_{a+b}=T^a(d_b)\circ(d_aP_b)\circ C_{a,b}:P_{a+b}\longrightarrow T^{a+b}.$$
The equality uses the canonical reassociation $T^a\circ T^b\cong T^{a+b}$ and holds on every object and morphism of $\mathcal C$.

proof.text: Work componentwise, with functional composition throughout. By [def-trf-endofunctor-powers], induction on $a$ identifies $T^a(T^bM)$ with $T^{a+b}M$: for $a=1$ this is the successor convention; the successor follows by applying $T$ to the preceding identification. The identical induction on a morphism $f$ identifies $T^a(T^b(f))$ with $T^{a+b}(f)$. These identifications have identity components; hence all reassociations below insert only identity arrows. The associativity and identity laws of [def-nagata-category] justify suppressing them.

proof.text:
Construct $d_r$ by induction on $r\geq1$. The initial $d_1$ is the identity natural isomorphism. If $d_r$ is natural, then for $f:M\to N$ its naturality and that of $C_{1,r}$ give
$$T^{r+1}(f)\circ T(d_r(M))\circ C_{1,r}(M)=T(d_r(N))\circ T(P_r(f))\circ C_{1,r}(M)=T(d_r(N))\circ C_{1,r}(N)\circ P_{r+1}(f).$$
Here $T$ preserves composition, and step 1 supplies the power convention. Thus the prescribed $d_{r+1}$ is natural. Its inverse at $M$ is $C_{1,r}(M)^{-1}\circ T(d_r(M)^{-1})$; both inverse identities follow by functoriality of $T$ and cancellation of each adjacent inverse pair. The inverse is natural as well: from $G(f)\circ u_M=u_N\circ F(f)$, composing on the left with $u_N^{-1}$ and on the right with $u_M^{-1}$ gives $F(f)\circ u_M^{-1}=u_N^{-1}\circ G(f)$. This proves that every $d_r$ is a natural isomorphism, without assuming that $T$ is an equivalence.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary positive $b$. Induct on the positive integer $a$, with claim $d_{a+b}=T^a(d_b)\circ(d_aP_b)\circ C_{a,b}$. At $a=1$, $d_1P_b$ is the identity and $T^1=T$, so the claim is exactly the defining recursion $d_{1+b}=T(d_b)\circ C_{1,b}$. This includes $b=1$.

proof.text:
Suppose the claim holds for $a\geq1$. Evaluate at any $M$ and expand the recursion and the induction hypothesis. Functoriality of $T$ yields
$$d_{a+1+b}(M)=T^{a+1}(d_b(M))\circ T(d_a(P_bM))\circ T(C_{a,b}(M))\circ C_{1,a+b}(M).$$
The assumed cocycle at the positive triple $(1,a,b)$ says
$$T(C_{a,b}(M))\circ C_{1,a+b}(M)=C_{1,a}(P_bM)\circ C_{a+1,b}(M).$$
Substitute this equality in the preceding expression. The two adjacent factors $T(d_a(P_bM))\circ C_{1,a}(P_bM)$ are precisely $d_{a+1}(P_bM)$ by its defining recursion evaluated at $P_bM$. The result is
$$d_{a+1+b}(M)=T^{a+1}(d_b(M))\circ d_{a+1}(P_bM)\circ C_{a+1,b}(M),$$
which is the successor claim. All equalities use only the given cocycle, recursion, functoriality, and the category laws [def-nagata-category]; the power identifications are those established in step 1.

proof.text: The induction proves the binary formula for every positive $a,b$ and every object $M$. Its right side is a natural transformation: applying the naturality equations of its three factors in succession, and using that $T^a$ preserves composition, moves any $P_{a+b}(f)$ through the composite and gives $T^{a+b}(f)$ at the other end. Equality at every component therefore is equality of natural transformations, including their compatibility with every morphism $f$. Together with step 2 this gives both assertions.
